meta.title: Leaderboard Competition
meta.subtitle: A competition between strategies, scored on risk-adjusted out-of-sample performance against the platform's own originated lines. Rewards go to the strategies that clear every validation gate, not to the ones that got lucky.
meta.cycle: 2026 regular season, from the Week 1 cycle open to the Week 18 cycle close, with an optional post-season cycle.
meta.state: Specification published. The live standings table is generated by scripts/compute_signals.py from the official datasets; it is empty or marked 'not evaluated' wherever the harness cannot yet evaluate a strategy.
meta.important_note: The platform originates its own lines. A strategy is therefore scored on whether it disagrees with the line model profitably, using signals that are deliberately different from the line model's own inputs. This is stated up front because a strategy evaluated against a reference it was fitted to would measure self-consistency rather than skill. See suggestion S-002 for the stronger design that is still open.

entrants.who: Any strategy registered in the platform's strategy register, submitted by the platform owner or by an invited participant. The entrant rules are open question Q-014.
entrants.one_strategy_per_entry: One strategy is one entry. A single entrant may register more than one strategy, but the correlation gate prevents near-duplicates from being rewarded twice.
submission_requirements: A written hypothesis and a precise signal definition that can be computed from official data.
The list of official inputs, with their source URLs.
A run through the validation harness that reports every gate.
Registration of the hypothesis in the hypothesis register, whether it passed or failed.

eligibility.rule: A strategy is eligible for scoring and reward only if it clears every gate G1 to G10. A failing gate is displayed with its measured value so the failure is legible, and the strategy is excluded from the reward pool.
eligibility.gate_table: Published on the Strategies page with the measured value for each strategy.
eligibility.ineligible_display: Ineligible strategies remain visible on the leaderboard, clearly marked, so that the competition cannot look selective.

scoring.primary_metric: Composite score, computed only over eligible strategies, from four normalised components.

components.name: Risk-adjusted return
components.definition: Net units divided by total units risked, divided by the standard deviation of per-bet units.
components.reason: Rewards efficiency of return rather than size of return, so that a strategy cannot win by over-sizing.

components.name: Drawdown control
components.definition: The negative of maximum peak-to-trough drawdown, measured as a fraction of the units staked.
components.reason: A strategy that survives is worth more than one that returns more before failing.

components.name: Out-of-sample sign consistency
components.definition: The share of evaluation folds in which the strategy's edge was positive, and the sign consistency across seasons.
components.reason: Consistency across independent periods is the clearest observable difference between skill and luck.

components.name: Skill share
components.definition: The share of observed outcome variance explained by the model's own probability, with its bootstrap interval.
components.reason: This is the component that operationalises the brief's instruction to remove luck from the equation.

scoring.normalisation: Each component is converted to a z-score across the eligible strategies for the cycle, then weighted and summed. The composite is then converted back to a readable scale for display.
tie_breaks: Earlier registration in the hypothesis register.
If still tied, the strategies are declared joint winners and the reward for that tier is split.
scoring.profit_is_not_a_component: Raw profit is deliberately excluded from the composite. A strategy is not rewarded for being large, only for being good.

rewards.structure: A tiered prize pool, split across the eligible strategies by composite rank.

tiers.eligibility: Eligible and ranked second, or first in its strategy class.
Eligible and ranked third, or first in its strategy class.
Eligible and ranked in the top quartile, or second in its strategy class.

rewards.per_class_awards: Each strategy class (single, parlay, prop, prop combo) is also scored on its own, with a class award, so that a strong prop strategy is not permanently outranked by a strong spread strategy.
rewards.pool_size: Not yet set. This is open question Q-013. Until the pool is published, the leaderboard is a scoreboard and not a funded competition.
rewards.transparency_rule: The reward schedule, the gate thresholds and the scoring weights are published before a cycle opens and are not changed during a cycle.

fair_play.hypothesis_register: Every hypothesis tested in a cycle is registered, whether it passed or failed, and the register is published at the cycle close. A cycle in which many hypotheses were tried and only one is shown is treated as a failed disclosure and is not scored.
fair_play.multiple_testing: A Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate control is applied across the register at the 10 per cent level, as gate G3.
fair_play.no_reuse: The same evaluation window may not be used to select a strategy and then to score it. The scoring window must follow the selection window.
fair_play.price_independence: A strategy may not use a commercial closing line, a projection service or any non-official feed. Every input must appear in the source manifest with an official URL.

current_state.evaluated_strategies: The single-bet class is evaluable from official standings and official results. The parlay, prop and prop-combination classes are registered but not yet evaluated, because they require per-game official player logs that the platform has not yet ingested.
current_state.next_milestone: Ingest official per-game box scores so the prop and prop-combination classes can be evaluated, then set the gate thresholds and open the first funded cycle.
